newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon arrests leftist labour leader.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon arrests leftist labour leader.

text.p: A Beirut prosecutor ordered the detention on Friday of leftist labour leader Elias Abou Rizk for interrogation on charges of impersonating the head of the General Labour Confederation (CGTL) and usurping office by force.
Prosecutor Abdallah Bitar issued the order after questioning Abou Rizk for three hours in connection with the charges, which were brought against him by rival labour leader Ghneim al-Zoghbi.

Bitar ordered Abou Rizk to be detained at the Courts of Justice pending further interrogation by an investigative magistrate who will decide whether he should stand trial. It was not immediately known when the new interrogation would take place.

Zoghbi and Abou Rizk have swapped accusations against each other since controversial CGTL elections last month which split the confederation and resulted in the election of separate leaderships headed by each of them.
Abou Rizk's supporters elected him in the morning and Ghneim's supporters elected him in the afternoon. Each says the election of the other was invalid.

The International Labour Organisation and the pan-Arab Workers Federation have recognised Abou Rizk's re-election and the International Confederation of Arab Trade Unions has refused to accept a member of the pro-Zoghbi leadership as Lebanon's representative.

However, the Lebanese government recognised Zoghbi's leadership. Abou Rizk, who was seeking re-election after heading the CGTL for the past four years, has been a thorn in the side of the government of billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri.

His leadership repeatedly called for pay rises, strikes and demonstrations and accused the government of ignoring the plight of the poor. In February 1996 the army imposed a curfew on much of the country to stop demonstrations called by Abou Rizk during a general strike.
